article_title: Beyond Predictive Learning Analytics Modelling and onto Explainable Artificial Intelligence with Prescriptive Analytics and ChatGPT
citation: Teo Susnjak. (2024). Beyond Predictive Learning Analytics Modelling and onto Explainable Artificial Intelligence with Prescriptive Analytics and ChatGPT. Int J Artif Intell Educ 34:452–482. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-023-00336-3
title: Cohort-relative z-score feature engineering converts raw academic and behavioural features into course-agnostic values for predictive modelling
description: This design pattern transforms raw behavioural and academic performance features (e.g., average grade, VLE resource access counts) into z-score standardised values relative to the learner's cohort, making them "more generic, contextually meaningful and comparable across different cohorts." The article states this conversion "converted the learner's absolute and mean values for a given feature into a form that captures the degree to which it deviates from the learner's cohort." The pattern increases descriptive power and model accuracy but trades off interpretability, which matters when features feed prescriptive feedback.
requirements: Access to cohort-level distributions of each feature to compute means and standard deviations
Domain knowledge to guide creation of derived features that amplify signal in the data
constraints: Z-score values possess greater descriptive power but come with the cost of lower interpretability, complicating Step 7's conversion back to raw values
target_learners: undergraduate learners across different cohorts and programmes
target_learning_goals: accurate prediction of programme completion outcomes across heterogeneous courses and programmes
examples: Engineered features marked in Table 1 include Grade Mark Deviation From Class Mean, Online Learning Pages Viewed Count Zscore, and Online Learning On Time Submission Count Zscore, all relativised to cohort totals
